purpose: derive the design constants from committed code and executed receipts so the manuscript can bind them, instead of restating them in prose
finding: the manuscript described a 32,000-token ceiling, a 12 tool-call ceiling and a 45-minute wall time as if they governed the executed work. They governed nothing: run_pilot.py, which built every executed episode, emits no ceiling fields; run_episode.py only type-checks that a configuration declares them and never enforces them; and no executed receipt records a token ceiling.

declared_but_not_enforced.enforcement: none; the values are type-checked and then unused

actually_applied_in_executed_blocks.wallclock_limit_source: the shell timeout used in the executed cost and variance runs

derived_from_receipts.variance_design: 4 frozen confirmation tasks x 4 conditions x 2 repeats = 32 episodes
derived_from_receipts.cost_design: one burned pilot task, two conditions, three repeats each, identical workspace digest within condition, transcripts written to files and verified complete

consequence: the manuscript sentence is corrected to separate the confirmatory protocol from what the executed instrument blocks actually applied, and the applied constants are bound to this receipt
